content:
sophia: quick heads-up — bringing up paperwing-v1 embeddings in the int6 lab. did a quick holdout recall run on lt-short-v2 (5k queries). recall@1 dropped from 0.895 -> 0.822 after per-tensor int6. per-channel int6 did better but still down.

liam: are these with or without index-time normalization? batch=1? seq len?

sophia: no idx-time norm, batch=1, seq<=8. results: float32 recall@1=0.895 -> int6 per-tensor 0.822; per-channel 0.841.

anya: breakdown by frequency? tail behaviour matters.

sophia: freq buckets: head(>=200): 0.92 -> 0.918; mid(20-199): 0.88 -> 0.86; tail(<20): 0.84 -> 0.68.

raj: that's a big tail impact. what about embedding norm shift and cosine spread?

sophia: mean L2 norm float32=0.98, int6=0.75. cosine histogram compressed toward 0.0, more collisions around 0.6-0.8 reduced.

liam: suggests dynamic range clipping is too aggressive. can you try per-channel scale + per-layer clipping + a light percentile clip (e.g., 99.5th)? also try cheap post-hoc L2-normalize on index vectors.

sophia: tried per-channel scaling -> recall@1 0.841. index-time L2-normalize of stored vectors (post-embed) brings recall@1 to 0.889. recall@10 also mostly recovers.

anya: nice. what's the latency and storage hit for index-time L2 normalize? we already L2 store sometimes.

sophia: storage no change (we overwrite with normalized vectors). latency on write path +0.9ms median. read path unchanged.

raj: so viable mitigation: either enable index-time norm in the embed pipeline or change quant scheme. ops-bot: pause rollout for paperwing-v1-int6 on staging.

ops-bot: rollout paused for paperwing-v1-int6 in staging — flagged by eng-ml (reason: recall@1 regression on lt-short-v2).

liam: next actions: a) run lt-longtail-aug w/ same configs b) test nf4 and 8bit-fp quant modes on same harness c) run per-query diff to identify common failure modes (e.g., stopwords, short noun phrases).

sophia: will push a small PR with harness, raw outputs, per-query diffs, and script to reproduce numbers. dropping the quick table here. cc @liam @anya @raj

--- numbers ---
float32: recall@1=0.895 recall@10=0.976 mean_norm=0.98
int6 (per-tensor): recall@1=0.822 recall@10=0.967 mean_norm=0.75
int6 (per-channel): recall@1=0.841 recall@10=0.971 mean_norm=0.89
int6 + idx-l2norm: recall@1=0.889 recall@10=0.975 mean_norm=1.00

liam: if idx-norm is cheap and robust we can expose it as an opt-in flag per-customer. run parity across languages too.

anya: agree; also run stratified precision@1 and nearest-neighbor label flips to see if specific query templates flip.

sophia: noted — will run those tomorrow and post results. :mag: :bar_chart: 

ops-bot: reminder to file an incident if this hits prod customers.

sophia: thanks all, will update thread when PR is ready.
